newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares edge down at noon, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares edge down at noon, mood cautious.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were slightly down at midday on Friday on shrinking volumes, with most investors sidelined waiting for a clearer direction, brokers said.
The B index edged down 0.238 points or 0.28 percent to 86.102 points on thin volume of 2.603 million shares worth $2.018 million.

Investors were taking a wait-and-see attitude for fear of new announcements of crackdown measures, brokers said. The issue of 230 million new B shares of Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co Ltd also attracted the attention of many investors.

"Major institutions want to let the market consolidate after pushing up the index over the past few days," one broker said. "They have shifted their capital in to buy Jinan Qingqi, which may bring them big profits after its listing."
Jinan Qingqi is issuing its B shares on Thursday and Friday at a price of $0.482 per share.
"The market will consolidate around 85-87 points for a while, but its upward momentum will not change," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 26 traded, with 11 down, seven flat and eight up.
Shanghai Haixin Co was the biggest loser on selling to unwind positions, slipping $0.032 or 4.64 percent to $0.658 on volume of 110,000 shares.

Pudong real estate Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded with some institutional cross trading, gaining $0.004 or 0.56 percent to $0.718 on volume of 504,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index was modestly up after the falls of the past few days, but trading was sluggish and the mood cautious, brokers said.
The index put on 1.244 points or 0.09 percent to 1,319.889 on volume of 152.5 million shares worth 2.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 19.166 points or 0.49 percent to 3,893.988 points.
Xiamen Motor Co was the star on institutional buying, rising 0.60 or 7.74 percent to 8.35 yuan on volume of 495,541 shares.
